approachQuestion.prompt:
Nearest service desk. A building has V rooms joined by undirected corridors. Every corridor takes one minute to walk. A nonempty list desks contains distinct room IDs. Return an array distance where distance[v] is the minimum walking time from room v to any desk, or -1 when no desk is reachable. A desk has distance zero.

The read-only adjacency lists are already built. IDs are 0 through V-1; 1 <= V <= 200000, 0 <= E <= 400000, 1 <= len(desks) <= V. There are no self-loops or duplicate edges; each edge is listed at both endpoints.

Example 1: lists=[[1],[0,2],[1,3],[2],[]], desks=[0,3], output=[0,1,1,0,-1].
Example 2: lists=[[1],[0]], desks=[0,1], output=[0,0].

options.text: Set every distance to -1. Give all desks distance zero and put them in one FIFO queue before exploring. Assign each unassigned neighbor a distance one larger when enqueuing it.
options.feedback: All desks begin in the same distance layer. The first discovery of a room therefore comes from a nearest desk; disconnected rooms remain unassigned.

options.text: Run a fresh breadth-first search from each desk and take the minimum distance for every room, keeping -1 only if all searches fail to reach it.
options.feedback: Every individual distance is correct and taking the minimum solves the full domain. However, the searches repeatedly explore the same corridors; one shared initial frontier removes that repetition.

options.text: Run breadth-first search from desks[0] and use its distance array as the answer.
options.feedback: In lists=[[1],[0]], desks=[0,1], this reports [0,1] instead of [0,0]. Another desk can be closer, including the room itself.

options.text: Put all desks at distance zero, then explore them with depth-first search, assigning each other room a distance only on its first visit.
options.feedback: Take lists=[[1,3],[0,2],[1,3],[0,2],[]], desks=[0,4]. If DFS follows 0-1-2-3 first, it assigns room 3 distance 3 even though corridor 0-3 gives distance 1. First discovery is minimal only with distance-layer ordering.

feedback.reason: Equal-cost routes to any member of a source set can share one ordered frontier initialized with every source.
details: Allocate the distance output initialized to -1. Assign zero to each desk and enqueue all desks in a preallocated FIFO queue. Repeatedly remove the front room and scan its neighbors. If a neighbor is still -1, assign the current distance plus one and enqueue it. Use the assigned distance itself as the visited marker. Leave unreached entries at -1.

Queue all desks initially at distance zero. Their waves expand together, assigning each room its closest desk distance at first discovery. Repeating a whole traversal separately per desk discards that shared frontier.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze all-desks-frontier as revealed. V is the total room count, E the undirected corridor count, and K=len(desks), with 1 <= K <= V. Initialize the returned distance array, and use a separate preallocated queue with capacity V and constant-time indexed enqueue/dequeue. Do not copy adjacency lists. Exclude the read-only input and returned distance array from auxiliary space; include the queue. There is no recursion, hashing, array shifting, or hidden per-operation copying.
constraints: Choose the tightest standard worst-case bound for the specified implementation.

options.text: O(V + E) time, O(V) auxiliary space
O(K(V + E)) time, O(V) auxiliary space
O(V + E) time, O(1) auxiliary space
O(V + E) time, O(V + E) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: One multi-source BFS scans the graph while retaining one frontier queue.
details: The option “O(V + E) time, O(V) auxiliary space” is tight: array initialization visits V rooms, desk initialization takes K <= V, each room enters the queue at most once, and at most 2E neighbor entries are examined. The separate queue reserves V slots even though the distance array is excluded as output. B repeats the work per desk, which this implementation avoids. The option “O(V + E) time, O(1) auxiliary space” omits the queue. The option “O(V + E) time, O(V + E) auxiliary space” counts edge storage even though the input is reused without copying.
